limitations: Real installed-PWA sharing on Android Chrome (the OS share sheet posting to the installed app) is A27 and remains NOT_RUN; A08 is proven by posting through the real service worker from the page, exactly as the plan's testability map specifies.

The OS share sheet, install prompt and installed-PWA behavior are browser/OS chrome and not automatable; installability (A11) is checked structurally (manifest + registered SW + complete precache + offline load), per the plan.

A09's real-clipboard half is chromium-only by the plan's platform table: Playwright's WebKit grants no clipboard permissions and navigator.clipboard.read() is platform-denied there. The recorded attempt (webkit-paste-probe.log) shows WebKit DOES accept clipboard.write(image) and DOES process a dispatched paste event carrying a file (review screen appears), so the paste-event channel works for real WebKit users; the Paste-button read channel cannot be automated there.

Offline OCR (a11_offline_ocr_after_first_load) proves the precached /ocr-assets/ route end to end in both engines on this machine; it does not measure cold-start disk-cache eviction, browser quota limits on other devices, or real-phone offline behavior (A27/A30 NOT_RUN).

The app shell precache is ~39.1 MB per session (13 ocr-assets files + the hashed app bundle + icons + manifest); Playwright contexts are ephemeral so each test context re-caches it — measured, not a device-quota claim.

A14 (zero network requests after the model cache exists) is S3; S2's request audit still asserts same-origin-only traffic and no post text in any request, URL, cookie, console or storage. The share-target POST body is consumed in memory by the service worker, handed to the page, and never cached or logged (asserted by the a08 cache-exactness check).
Service-worker update behavior (a new deploy taking over an open tab) is not exercised: each test context is fresh, so only first-install + activate + claim are covered.

The dispatch of synthetic ClipboardEvent('paste') measures the app's paste routing; a real Ctrl/Cmd+V with an image requires OS-level clipboard automation that Playwright does not offer — recorded honestly rather than faked.
